metadata.specialty: Urology; male sexual and reproductive health
metadata.summary: This update summarises the European Association of Urology guidance on evaluating, treating and following up male infertility. It covers semen, hormonal, genetic and imaging assessments, as well as management of specific conditions and options for medical treatment, surgery and fertility preservation. It emphasises assessment of both partners and shared decisions that account for the female partner’s fertility status.

conditions_covered: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD)
Germ cell malignancy and male infertility
care_settings: Dedicated late-effects clinic and survivorship programme
target_population: Men seeking medical help for fertility problems
Couples who have not conceived after 12 consecutive months of regular, unprotected intercourse
Men with abnormal semen parameters and their female partners
therapeutic_areas: Transurethral resection of the ejaculatory ducts (TURED)

toxicities.event: Impaired semen quality and spermatogenesis following cancer treatment
recognition: Treatment for TGCT can further impair semen quality.
Spermatogenesis usually recovers 1–4 yr after chemotherapy.
prevention: Offer sperm cryopreservation before gonadotoxic treatment or ablative surgery that could impair spermatogenesis or ejaculation.

toxicities.event: Increased sperm aneuploidy following gonadotoxic treatment
recognition: Sperm aneuploidy may remain elevated for up to 2 yr following treatment.
Levels often return to pretreatment values 18–24 mo after treatment.

toxicities.event: Sperm DNA damage and increased SDF
recognition: Chemotherapy is associated with sperm DNA damage and higher SDF.

prevention: Use contraception throughout treatment and for at least 6 mo after its completion.

toxicities.event: Hypogonadism after treatment for testicular cancer
recognition: Survivors of testicular cancer have an increased risk of hypogonadism; risk is greatest at 6–12 mo after treatment.
Men with TGCT also have Leydig cell dysfunction, including in the contralateral testis.

management.severity: Continuous signs or symptoms of testosterone deficiency
management.actions: Evaluate serum testosterone during management. It is reasonable to defer testosterone therapy until signs or symptoms of deficiency persist, because Leydig cell function may improve after treatment.

toxicities.event: Haematoma and testicular fibrosis after sperm retrieval
recognition: Haematoma and fibrosis were reported less frequently after mTESE than after cTESE.

toxicities.event: Complications following transurethral resection of the ejaculatory ducts
recognition: Potential complications include epididymitis, treatment failure, urinary incontinence, and reflux of urine into the ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles.
prevention: Counsel patients about these potential complications before TURED.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Offer sperm cryopreservation before planned orchidectomy or other oncological treatment that could impair spermatogenesis or ejaculation. Preservation of ejaculated semen should be offered; surgically retrieved sperm is an option for severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia.
prophylaxis.target_population: Men with cancer before gonadotoxic agents or ablative surgery

prophylaxis.recommendation: Use contraception because chemotherapy and radiotherapy are teratogenic.
prophylaxis.duration: During treatment and for at least 6 mo after completion

prophylaxis.recommendation: Treat cryptorchidism between the age of 6 mo and 18 mo to preserve future spermatogenesis and hormone production and reduce tumour risk; surgery is the most effective approach.
Encourage regular testicular self-examination because testicular cancer risk remains elevated, including after early orchidopexy.
prophylaxis.target_population: Men with a history of cryptorchidism

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise testicular self-examination, even when additional risk factors are absent, as it may permit earlier detection of TGCT.

infection_management.prevention: Refer sexual partners for assessment and treatment when a sexually transmitted cause is known or suspected.
infection_management.management: Treat the infection; sperm quality may improve, but the probability of conception does not necessarily increase. For suspected genitourinary tract infection, perform semen culture or polymerase chain reaction analysis for common urinary tract pathogens.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Chronic bacterial prostatitis (type II according to the National Institutes of Health classification)
infection_management.management: Antibiotic therapy has provided symptom relief, eradication of micro-organisms, and reductions in cellular and humoral inflammatory findings in urogenital secretions.
Although antibiotics might improve sperm quality, there is no evidence that treating CP/CPPS increases the likelihood of natural conception.

A peroxidase-positive white blood cell level of >106/ml of ejaculate indicates inflammation but does not necessarily indicate infection. There is currently no evidence that treating leukocytospermia alone, without evidence of infective organisms, improves conception rates.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Ureaplasma urealyticum and Myocoplasma hominis infections
infection_management.management: A meta-analysis reported an association of these strains with male infertility; the document does not specify treatment for either infection.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Ureoplasma parvum and Mycoplasma genitalium infections
infection_management.management: The cited meta-analysis did not find an association of these strains with male infertility; the document does not specify treatment.
An association with male infertility is emerging, but prospective validation is limited and whether antiviral treatment improves fertility outcomes is unclear.
A cited casecontrol study suggested that treatment may improve sperm parameters; whether it improves conception rates remains unclear.

therapies_index.name: lifestyle changes
approved_indications: Infertile men should be advised to improve modifiable lifestyle factors to increase their chances of conception.
therapies_index.administration: Measures discussed include weight loss, physical exercise, smoking cessation, and reduction of high alcohol intake.

therapies_index.name: antioxidants
approved_indications: They may be considered empirical treatment for male infertility, but the guideline advises against routine use in idiopathic infertility.

therapies_index.name: prebiotics/probiotics
approved_indications: Supplementation has been studied in idiopathic male infertility, but the guideline advises against routine treatment for this indication.

therapies_index.name: gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
approved_indications: It has been studied as medical treatment for cryptorchidism, with poor success rates; hormonal treatment for cryptorchidism in postpubertal men is discouraged.

therapies_index.name: hCG
approved_indications: Drug treatment to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.
It has been studied as medical treatment for cryptorchidism, with poor success rates.

therapies_index.name: hCG with or without FSH
approved_indications: A cited meta-analysis assessed this approach for sperm production in patients with NOA and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

therapies_index.name: human menopausal gonadotropins
approved_indications: Drug treatment to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.

therapies_index.name: recombinant FSH
approved_indications: Drug treatment to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.

therapies_index.name: highly purified FSH
approved_indications: Drug treatment to induce spermatogenesis in men with congenital or acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism who wish to conceive.

therapies_index.name: FSH
approved_indications: Treatment to increase spermatogenesis in men with idiopathic oligozoospermia whose FSH values are within the normal range; high-dose FSH is discouraged for idiopathic infertility.
Hormonal stimulation before TESE in men with NOA has been investigated, but routine use is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: selective oestrogen receptor modulators
therapies_index.mechanism: Blocking hypothalamic oestrogen receptors stimulates GnRH secretion and pituitary gonadotropin release, with potential stimulation of spermatogenesis.
approved_indications: Their use in idiopathic male infertility remains inconclusive, and routine treatment is discouraged.
They may be considered to induce spermatogenesis after anabolic steroid withdrawal in infertile men.

therapies_index.name: aromatase inhibitors
therapies_index.mechanism: They may reduce oestrogen production through reversible inhibition of cytochrome p450 isoenzymes 2A6 and 2C19 of the aromatase enzyme complex, reducing hypothalamic oestrogen feedback and increasing pituitary stimulation of FSH production.
approved_indications: They have been reported as an off-label option in male infertility, but routine treatment of idiopathic infertility is discouraged.

therapies_index.name: testolactone
approved_indications: It was studied as a steroidal aromatase inhibitor in infertile men; the guideline advises against routine aromatase inhibitor treatment for idiopathic infertility.

therapies_index.name: anastrozole
approved_indications: It was studied as a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in infertile men; the guideline advises against routine aromatase inhibitor treatment for idiopathic infertility.

therapies_index.name: letrozole
approved_indications: It was studied as a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in infertile men; the guideline advises against routine aromatase inhibitor treatment for idiopathic infertility.

therapies_index.name: testosterone therapy
approved_indications: Treatment for symptomatic patients with primary or secondary hypogonadism who are not considering parenthood; it must not be used to treat male infertility.

therapies_index.name: dopamine agonist therapy
approved_indications: Men with proven hyperprolactinaemia may be offered this treatment to improve sperm quality.

therapies_index.name: anabolic steroids
approved_indications: The guideline addresses their withdrawal in infertile men rather than recommending their use as infertility treatment.
therapies_index.administration: Withdraw for 6–12 mo before considering selective oestrogen receptor modulators or gonadotrophin therapy to induce spermatogenesis.

therapies_index.name: orchidopexy
approved_indications: Surgical treatment of childhood cryptorchidism is recommended between the age of 6 mo and 18 mo.
Unilateral or bilateral orchidopexy may be offered when technically feasible to adults with an undescended testis and biochemical hypogonadism and/or spermatogenic failure.
therapies_index.administration: When an undescended testis is corrected in adulthood, the guideline recommends a simultaneous testicular biopsy to assess for intratubular germ cell neoplasia in situ.
monitoring: Men with a history of cryptorchidism should be encouraged to perform regular testicular self-examinations.

therapies_index.name: orchidectomy
approved_indications: It should be offered to adult men with a unilateral undescended testis and normal hormonal function and spermatogenesis.
It may be offered after multidisciplinary discussion when testicular microcalcification is accompanied by a lesion with suspicious examination or US findings.
It is used in treatment of TGCT.
key_toxicities: Ablative surgery may impair spermatogenesis or ejaculation.

therapies_index.name: testicular biopsy
approved_indications: It is recommended during adult correction of undescended testes to detect intratubular germ cell neoplasia in situ.
It may be offered to infertile men with TM who have the specified additional risk factors.
It may be considered when TM is accompanied by a suspicious lesion, following multidisciplinary discussion.
therapies_index.administration: At orchidectomy for TGCT, biopsy of the contralateral testis should be offered to patients at high risk for GCNIS.

therapies_index.name: varicocelectomy
approved_indications: Surgery is recommended for adolescents with a persistently small testis associated with varicocele when the size difference is >2 ml or 20% and is confirmed on two subsequent visits performed 6 mo apart.
Treatment is recommended for infertile men with a clinical varicocele and abnormal semen parameters when infertility is otherwise unexplained and the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
It may be considered for elevated sperm DNA fragmentation with otherwise unexplained infertility or after failure of assisted reproductive techniques.
Treatment is discouraged for infertile men with normal semen analysis and for men with a subclinical varicocele.
therapies_index.administration: A microsurgical approach is discussed, but the guideline states that evidence is insufficient to establish one technique as definitively superior.
monitoring: The average time to improved semen parameters after repair is up to two spermatogenic cycles; spontaneous pregnancy was reported between 6 and 12 mo after varicocelectomy.

therapies_index.name: antibiotics
approved_indications: Antibiotic treatment of chronic bacterial prostatitis has provided symptom relief, microorganism eradication, and reduced inflammatory parameters.
Treatment of male accessory-gland infections may improve sperm quality but does not necessarily increase the probability of conception.
There is no evidence that treatment of CP/CPPS increases the probability of natural conception.

therapies_index.name: sperm cryopreservation
approved_indications: It should be offered before planned orchidectomy or gonadotoxic or ablative cancer treatment that may impair spermatogenesis or ejaculation.
therapies_index.administration: Preservation of ejaculated semen is presented as the most cost-effective approach; surgically retrieved sperm may be preserved in severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia.

therapies_index.name: onco-TESE
approved_indications: It should be offered to men with testicular cancer and azoospermia or severe semen abnormalities.
therapies_index.administration: Performed at the time of radical orchidectomy.

therapies_index.name: chemotherapy
approved_indications: It is mentioned as oncological treatment for which fertility preservation and contraception are relevant.
key_toxicities: Chemotherapy is described as teratogenic and is associated with DNA damage and increased SDF; gonadotoxic treatment may further impair semen quality.
monitoring: Contraception must be used during treatment and for at least 6 mo after completion.

therapies_index.name: radiotherapy
approved_indications: It is mentioned as oncological treatment for which fertility preservation and contraception are relevant.
key_toxicities: Radiotherapy is described as teratogenic; gonadotoxic treatment may further impair semen quality.
monitoring: Contraception must be used during treatment and for at least 6 mo after completion.

therapies_index.name: retroperitoneal surgery
approved_indications: It is mentioned as oncological surgery before which sperm cryopreservation should be offered.
key_toxicities: It may impair spermatogenesis or ejaculation.

therapies_index.name: vasoepididymostomy
approved_indications: It is given as an example of microsurgical reconstruction for epididymal or inguinal vasal obstruction.

therapies_index.name: microsurgical vasovasostomy
approved_indications: It is recommended for azoospermia caused by vasal or epididymal obstruction when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.

therapies_index.name: epididymovasostomy
approved_indications: It is recommended for azoospermia caused by vasal or epididymal obstruction when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.

therapies_index.name: vasectomy reversal
approved_indications: It may treat vas deferens obstruction following vasectomy.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline discusses a microsurgical technique.

therapies_index.name: microsurgical epididymal sperm aspiration
approved_indications: Sperm retrieval for obstructive azoospermia, including when reconstruction is unsuitable, ovarian reserve is limited, or the couple prefers direct ICSI treatment.

therapies_index.name: PESA
approved_indications: Percutaneous sperm retrieval for obstructive azoospermia, either alongside reconstruction or when reconstruction is unsuitable or not preferred.

therapies_index.name: TESA
approved_indications: Percutaneous sperm retrieval is listed among options for obstructive azoospermia; TESA is discouraged in patients with NOA.

therapies_index.name: TESE
approved_indications: It is required for intratesticular obstruction and is an option for sperm retrieval in other forms of obstructive azoospermia.
Surgical sperm retrieval may be performed in men with NOA who are candidates for ICSI, but must not be performed when complete deletions include AZFa and AZFb.

Use of testicular sperm for ICSI may be considered experimentally and case by case when ejaculated sperm has high SDF, after common risk factors have been excluded and other measures to reduce SDF have failed.

therapies_index.name: cTESE
approved_indications: It is discussed as a surgical sperm retrieval technique for NOA, although the panel favours mTESE on low-quality evidence.
therapies_index.administration: It uses random testicular biopsies to retrieve sperm.
key_toxicities: It has been associated with more complications than other retrieval techniques; haematoma and fibrosis were less frequent with mTESE in comparative observations.
monitoring: Long-term follow-up has observed recovery of baseline testosterone levels after the procedure.

therapies_index.name: mTESE
approved_indications: It is the panel's preferred surgical sperm retrieval approach for NOA, based on low-quality evidence.
Salvage mTESE has been studied after unsuccessful cTESE or testicular sperm aspiration.
therapies_index.administration: Operative microscopy is used to identify seminiferous tubules more likely to contain sperm while limiting tissue sampling and inadvertent vascular injury.
key_toxicities: Haematoma and fibrosis have been observed less often than after cTESE.
monitoring: Long-term follow-up has observed recovery of baseline testosterone levels after the procedure.

therapies_index.name: ICSI
approved_indications: It is discussed as an assisted reproductive option using retrieved sperm in azoospermia.
Use of testicular sperm in patients with high ejaculated-sperm SDF may be considered an experimental option after counselling.
Men with Yq microdeletion and their partners should be informed before proceeding that the microdeletion will be passed on to sons.

therapies_index.name: intrauterine insemination
approved_indications: It is mentioned as an assisted reproductive treatment assessed in studies of FSH administration for idiopathic infertility.

therapies_index.name: TURED
approved_indications: It may treat ejaculatory duct obstruction caused by postinflammatory or cystic blockage.
therapies_index.administration: The ejaculatory ducts are resected transurethrally.
key_toxicities: Potential complications include epididymitis, treatment failure, urinary incontinence, and reflux of urine into the ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles.

recommendations.statement: Obtain at least two consecutive semen analyses when the initial result is abnormal.

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely measure reactive oxygen species when diagnosing or managing the male partner of an infertile couple.
recommendations.rationale: Routine measurement lacks a standardised method and requires validation.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Perform SDF testing for couples with recurrent pregnancy loss after natural conception or failure of ART, and for men with unexplained infertility.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Consider testicular sperm for ICSI as an experimental option when ejaculated sperm has high SDF.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence for this approach is limited.

recommendations.statement: In every case of oligozoospermia or azoospermia, perform hormonal testing that includes at least serum total testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone/luteinising hormone.

recommendations.statement: Offer standard karyotype analysis and genetic counselling for diagnostic purposes to every man with azoospermia or oligozoospermia (spermatozoa <5 million/ml).
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Provide men with Klinefelter syndrome with long-term endocrine follow-up and appropriate medical treatment.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Test for Y-chromosome microdeletions in men with sperm concentrations of 1 million sperm/ml; consider testing when sperm concentrations are <5 million sperm/ml.
recommendations.context: The recommendation table gives 1 million sperm/ml without a comparison sign.

recommendations.statement: Advise men with Yq microdeletion and their partners who wish to pursue ICSI that sons will inherit the microdeletions.

recommendations.statement: Do not undertake testicular sperm extraction in patients whose complete deletions include the AZFa and AZFb regions.
recommendations.rationale: Complete deletions of these regions predict a poor outcome for surgical sperm retrieval.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Test men with structural abnormalities of the vas deferens, whether unilateral or bilateral absence without renal anomalies, and their partners for CFTR gene mutations.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Offer genetic counselling to every couple in whom clinical or genetic investigation identifies a genetic abnormality, and to patients carrying a potentially inheritable disease.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Perform scrotal US in infertile men.
recommendations.rationale: Infertile men have an increased risk of testis cancer.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Discuss invasive diagnostic options, including US-guided testicular biopsy with frozen section, radical orchidectomy, and surveillance, within a multidisciplinary team for infertile men whose testicular lesions are indeterminate on US.
recommendations.context: This discussion is particularly relevant when additional malignancy risk factors are present.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Perform transrectal US when partial or complete distal obstruction is suspected.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 4 – Recommendations for diagnostic workup of male infertility

recommendations.statement: Do not treat cryptorchidism hormonally in postpubertal men.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: When correcting undescended testes in adulthood, perform a simultaneous testicular biopsy to detect intratubular germ cell neoplasia in situ (formerly carcinoma in situ).
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Offer orchidectomy to adult men who have a unilateral undescended testis and normal hormonal function and spermatogenesis.
recommendations.rationale: An undescended testis carries an increased risk of testicular cancer and GCNIS.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: If technically feasible, offer unilateral or bilateral orchidopexy to adults with unilateral or bilateral undescended testes and biochemical hypogonadism and/or spermatogenic failure (ie, infertility).
recommendations.rationale: Orchidopexy may preserve androgen production and fertility.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Advise men with TM to examine their testes themselves, even if they have no additional risk factors.
recommendations.rationale: Self-examination may help detect TGCT early.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: In men with isolated TM and no associated risk factors, do not perform testicular biopsy, follow-up scrotal US, biochemical tumour marker testing, or abdominal or pelvic computed tomography.
recommendations.context: Examples of associated risk factors are infertility, cryptorchidism, testicular cancer, and atrophic testis.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Offer testicular biopsy to infertile men with TM who are in a higher-risk group: spermatogenic failure (infertility), bilateral TM, atrophic testes (<12 ml), a history of undescended testes, or TGCT.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: For patients with TM and associated lesions that have suspicious findings on physical examination or US, perform inguinal surgical exploration with testicular biopsy or offer orchidectomy after multidisciplinary team review and discussion with the patient.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Manage men previously treated for TGCT through a multidisciplinary team with a dedicated late-effects clinic and survivorship programme.
recommendations.rationale: These men face increased risks of hypogonadism, sexual dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Cryopreserve sperm before a planned orchidectomy or further neoadjuvant or adjuvant cancer treatment.
recommendations.rationale: Cancer treatments may impair fertility.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Offer onco-TESE during radical orchidectomy to men with testicular cancer who have azoospermia or severe abnormalities in semen parameters.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Offer adolescents surgery for varicocele when a persistently small testis has a size difference of >2 ml or 20%, confirmed at two subsequent visits performed 6 mo apart.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Do not treat varicocele in infertile men with a normal semen analysis or in men whose varicocele is subclinical.
recommendations.rationale: Studies found no benefit of treatment over observation in populations consisting mainly of men with normal semen parameters, and treatment of subclinical varicocele did not improve spontaneous pregnancy chances.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Treat infertile men who have a clinical varicocele and abnormal semen parameters when the couple’s infertility is otherwise unexplained and the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
recommendations.rationale: Treatment is intended to improve fertility rates.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Consider varicocelectomy for men with elevated sperm DNA fragmentation and otherwise unexplained infertility, or after failure of assisted reproductive techniques, including recurrent pregnancy loss or failure of embryogenesis or implantation.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence concerning pregnancy and live birth benefits in these settings remains limited.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Treat male accessory-gland infections.
recommendations.rationale: Treatment may improve sperm quality but does not necessarily increase the likelihood of conception.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Refer sexual partners of patients whose accessory sex gland infections are known or suspected to result from sexually transmitted diseases for evaluation and treatment.
recommendations.source_heading: Table 5 – Recommendations for specific male infertility conditions

recommendations.statement: Explain to infertile men how obesity, low physical activity, smoking, and high alcohol intake adversely affect sperm quality and testosterone levels, and advise them to improve these lifestyle factors to increase their chances of conception.

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely use antioxidants, prebiotics/probiotics, selective oestrogen receptor modulators, or aromatase inhibitors to treat idiopathic infertility.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence is insufficient to support routine use of these empirical treatments.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation against postpubertal hormonal treatment is graded Strong.

recommended_regimens.name: Testicular biopsy
recommended_regimens.summary: Perform biopsy at the time of adult correction to detect intratubular germ cell neoplasia in situ.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Panel consensus supports multiple biopsies of a unilateral undescended testis during orchidopexy to exclude GCNIS.

treatment_pathways.condition: Germ cell malignancy and male infertility

decision_rules: Discuss fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment.
Offer preservation of ejaculated sperm; consider surgically retrieved sperm when azoospermia or severe semen abnormalities prevent that approach.
Use contraception during chemotherapy or radiotherapy and for at least 6 mo after treatment.

recommended_regimens.summary: Preserve sperm before planned orchidectomy or additional neoadjuvant or adjuvant oncological treatment; ejaculated semen is the preferred preservation strategy when available.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Before planned orchidectomy or gonadotoxic treatment

recommended_regimens.summary: Offer surgical sperm retrieval during radical orchidectomy to men with testicular cancer and azoospermia or severe abnormalities of semen parameters.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: At the time of radical orchidectomy

supportive_care: Provide fertility-preservation counselling before gonadotoxic treatment.
Use contraception during chemotherapy and radiotherapy and for at least 6 mo after their completion.

treatment_pathways.condition: Germ cell malignancy and male infertility

decision_rules: Arrange multidisciplinary survivorship care for late effects.
Assess serum testosterone during management; consider postponing testosterone therapy until signs or symptoms of deficiency persist.

recommended_regimens.summary: Provide multidisciplinary follow-up because survivors have increased risks of hypogonadism, sexual dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease.

recommended_regimens.summary: Advise men with TM to examine their testes themselves to support early TGCT detection.

recommended_regimens.name: Testicular biopsy
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer tissue assessment to higher-risk infertile men with TM.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The association between TM and TGCT is described as controversial; risk factors help identify men who may harbour GCNIS.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with TM and an associated lesion suspicious on physical examination or US

recommended_regimens.name: Inguinal surgical exploration with testicular biopsy
recommended_regimens.summary: Investigate a suspicious associated lesion surgically after multidisciplinary discussion.

recommended_regimens.summary: Operate for varicocele associated with a confirmed, persistent difference in testicular size.

decision_rules: Treat a clinical varicocele in this population to improve fertility rates.

recommended_regimens.summary: Treat the clinical varicocele after considering the couple's fertility circumstances.

not_recommended.reason: Treatment was not effective at increasing spontaneous pregnancy chances.

not_recommended.reason: Randomised studies involving mainly men with normal semen parameters showed no benefit favouring treatment over observation.

response_assessment.interpretation: This is the reported average time to improvement.
This is the reported interval during which spontaneous pregnancy occurs.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The microsurgical approach was associated with the lowest complication and recurrence rates and the highest spontaneous pregnancy rates, but the data were too limited to establish that any technique is definitively superior.

alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Elevated SDF with otherwise unexplained infertility, or failure of assisted reproductive techniques

alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: NOA with a clinically significant varicocele after discussion of risks, benefits, and the female partner's ovarian reserve

supportive_care: Explain that the evidence for improved sperm retrieval in this population is of low quality.

recommended_regimens.summary: For chronic bacterial prostatitis, antibiotic treatment has relieved symptoms, eradicated micro-organisms, and reduced inflammatory measures in urogenital secretions.

response_assessment.interpretation: These are the benefits reported for antibiotic therapy of chronic bacterial prostatitis.

recommended_regimens.summary: An effective drug option named for inducing spermatogenesis in this population.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The document does not specify a dose, schedule, or preferred choice among the named effective drug options.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with idiopathic oligozoospermia and FSH values within the normal range
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: FSH values within the normal range (generally 1.5–8 mIU/ml)
decision_rules: Use FSH to increase spermatogenesis in the specified population; do not treat idiopathic infertility with high-dose FSH.

recommended_regimens.name: FSH
recommended_regimens.summary: Use treatment to increase spermatogenesis when FSH is within the normal range.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The cited studies collectively suggest a dose-dependent, significant increase in sperm concentration and total sperm count, as well as significant increases in spontaneous and ART pregnancy rates.

not_recommended.name: High-dose FSH
not_recommended.reason: The guideline advises against its use for idiopathic infertility.

response_assessment.method: Sperm concentration and total sperm count
response_assessment.interpretation: These are the spermatogenesis measures reported to improve in the cited studies.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation against high-dose FSH is graded Weak.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men undergoing treatment for infertility
decision_rules: Do not use testosterone therapy as treatment for male infertility.

not_recommended.name: Testosterone therapy
not_recommended.reason: The guideline explicitly advises against its use to treat male infertility.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation against testosterone therapy for male infertility is graded Strong.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Symptomatic men with primary or secondary hypogonadism who are not considering parenthood
decision_rules: Provide testosterone therapy for symptomatic hypogonadism only in the stated population that is not considering parenthood.

recommended_regimens.name: Testosterone therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat symptomatic primary or secondary hypogonadism in men not considering parenthood.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with proven hyperprolactinaemia
decision_rules: Offer a dopamine agonist to improve sperm quality.

recommended_regimens.name: Dopamine agonist therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer treatment when hyperprolactinaemia is established.

response_assessment.interpretation: Improvement is the stated treatment objective.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Infertile men using anabolic steroids
decision_rules: Withdraw anabolic steroids before considering medication to induce spermatogenesis.

recommended_regimens.name: Withdrawal of anabolic steroids
recommended_regimens.summary: Stop anabolic steroids before considering selective oestrogen receptor modulators or gonadotrophin therapy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline presents selective oestrogen receptor modulators and gonadotrophin therapy as options to consider after withdrawal, not as treatments to begin immediately.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with intratesticular obstruction who are pursuing fertility treatment
decision_rules: Use testicular sperm retrieval when the obstruction is intratesticular.

recommended_regimens.name: TESE
recommended_regimens.summary: Retrieve sperm surgically for intratesticular obstruction.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The female partner's ovarian reserve should inform decisions about sperm retrieval and ICSI whenever reconstruction is being considered.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with azoospermia due to vasal or epididymal obstruction whose female partner has good ovarian reserve
decision_rules: Offer microsurgical reconstruction for amenable vasal or epididymal obstruction when the female partner has good ovarian reserve.
Sperm retrieval can supplement reconstruction or replace it when repair is unsuitable, ovarian reserve is limited, or the couple prefers direct ICSI.

recommended_regimens.name: Microsurgical vasovasostomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Reconstruct a vasal obstruction in the specified couple.

recommended_regimens.name: Epididymovasostomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Use microsurgical reconstruction for an amenable epididymal obstruction.

alternative_regimens.name: Microsurgical epididymal sperm aspiration
alternative_regimens.summary: Retrieve epididymal sperm for ICSI, either alongside reconstruction or instead of it.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Reconstruction is unsuitable, the partner's ovarian reserve is limited, or the couple prefers direct ICSI; retrieval may also supplement reconstruction.

alternative_regimens.name: PESA
alternative_regimens.summary: Use percutaneous epididymal sperm retrieval as an option for ICSI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Retrieval is selected instead of, or alongside, reconstruction.

alternative_regimens.name: TESE
alternative_regimens.summary: Use testicular sperm retrieval as an option for ICSI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Retrieval is selected instead of, or alongside, reconstruction.

alternative_regimens.name: TESA
alternative_regimens.summary: Use percutaneous testicular sperm retrieval as an option for ICSI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Retrieval is selected instead of, or alongside, reconstruction.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation supporting retrieval techniques under the stated circumstances is graded Strong. The document reports comparable ICSI pregnancy outcomes for epididymal versus testicular sperm and for fresh versus frozen–thawed epididymal sperm.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with vas deferens obstruction after vasectomy
decision_rules: Consider reversal of vasectomy when reconstruction is appropriate, taking the female partner's ovarian reserve into account.

recommended_regimens.name: Vasectomy reversal
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat postvasectomy obstruction with microsurgical reversal.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The microsurgical technique has a successful patency rate of 90–97%.

alternative_regimens.name: Sperm retrieval and ICSI
alternative_regimens.summary: Proceed directly to sperm retrieval and ICSI instead of reconstruction when appropriate.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Limited ovarian reserve, a preference against reconstruction, or a couple's preference for direct ICSI

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with ejaculatory duct obstruction due to postinflammatory or cystic obstruction
decision_rules: Consider transurethral treatment of the obstructed ejaculatory ducts and discuss its potential complications.

recommended_regimens.name: TURED
recommended_regimens.summary: Transurethrally resect the ejaculatory ducts to treat postinflammatory or cystic obstruction.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The reported pregnancy rate after TURED is 12.5–31%.

supportive_care: Counsel about epididymitis, treatment failure, urinary incontinence, and urine reflux into the ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with NOA who are candidates for ART, specifically ICSI
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Exclude complete AZFa and AZFb microdeletions before surgical sperm retrieval.
decision_rules: Confirm NOA on two consecutive semen analyses when centrifugation reveals no sperm.
Assess medical history, hormones, genetics, and scrotal US before treatment.
Perform surgical sperm retrieval for men proceeding to ICSI; favour microdissection TESE, while recognising the low quality of comparative evidence.
Do not use FNA, TESA, or prognostic FNA mapping in this population.

recommended_regimens.name: microdissection TESE
recommended_regimens.summary: Use as the panel's preferred surgical sperm-retrieval approach for NOA.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: One meta-analysis reported successful sperm extraction 1.5 times more often with mTESE than cTESE; another found comparable retrieval rates. The document reports positive sperm retrieval after TESE in up to 50% of patients with NOA, with wide variation between cohorts and techniques.

alternative_regimens.name: conventional TESE
alternative_regimens.summary: A surgical retrieval technique assessed alongside microdissection TESE; the panel favours the latter because complications appear less frequent.

not_recommended.name: FNA
not_recommended.reason: The guideline advises against it for patients with NOA.

not_recommended.name: TESA
not_recommended.reason: The guideline advises against it for patients with NOA.

not_recommended.name: FNA mapping
not_recommended.reason: The guideline advises against its use as a prognostic procedure before definitive TESE; mapping does not itself retrieve sperm and may require an additional operation and delay treatment.

not_recommended.name: Surgical sperm retrieval with complete AZFa and AZFb microdeletions
not_recommended.reason: The guideline states that the chance of sperm retrieval is zero.

response_assessment.interpretation: Preoperative biochemical and clinical variables are not sufficiently reliable to predict retrieval success.

supportive_care: Provide genetic counselling before ART to couples with genetic abnormalities.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Surgical retrieval for eligible men and the prohibitions on FNA, TESA, and retrieval with complete AZFa and AZFb microdeletions are graded Strong. The prohibition on prognostic FNA mapping is graded Weak. Comparative evidence for microdissection TESE is limited by a paucity of RCTs.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with NOA after unsuccessful conventional TESE or testicular sperm aspiration
decision_rules: Consider salvage microdissection TESE after a previous unsuccessful retrieval attempt.

alternative_regimens.name: salvage mTESE
alternative_regimens.summary: The document reports successful sperm retrieval after a previous failed cTESE or testicular sperm aspiration.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Previous failed cTESE or testicular sperm aspiration

response_assessment.interpretation: Reported data showed successful retrieval in 46.5% of patients with a previous failed cTESE or testicular sperm aspiration.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The 46.5% result is reported study data, not a separately graded salvage recommendation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with NOA being considered for hormonal stimulation before TESE, including men with hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism
decision_rules: Do not begin hormonal stimulation before TESE outside clinical trials.
Do not routinely use medical stimulation before conventional or microdissection TESE in NOA with hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism.

not_recommended.name: Hormonal stimulation before TESE outside clinical trials
not_recommended.reason: No RCT has shown improved sperm retrieval in idiopathic NOA, and a standardised protocol is lacking.

not_recommended.name: Routine medical therapy before conventional or microdissection TESE in NOA with hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism
not_recommended.reason: A meta-analysis suggested a possible retrieval benefit in eugonadal men but not in those with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism; its included studies had moderate or severe risk of bias.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Both recommendations against these uses are graded Weak. The document says randomised studies are needed to confirm the meta-analysis findings.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Fully informed men with high SDF in ejaculated sperm who are proceeding to ICSI
decision_rules: Consider testicular sperm for ICSI only as an experimental, individualised option.
First exclude common risk factors for elevated SDF and establish that other treatments to reduce SDF have failed.
Discuss the low level of evidence with the patient and reproductive specialists.

alternative_regimens.name: Testicular sperm for ICSI
alternative_regimens.summary: Offer as an experimental option on a case-by-case basis after the specified evaluation and counselling.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: High SDF in ejaculated sperm, exclusion of common risk factors, failure of other SDF-reducing treatments, and fully informed consent

supportive_care: Include reproductive specialists in the discussion and explain the low level of evidence.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation to consider this experimental option is graded Weak. A cited meta-analysis suggested improved ART outcomes with TESE for ICSI but had significant data heterogeneity and called for validating RCTs.

conditions.name: Male infertility
conditions.description: Infertility is the failure of a sexually active couple to achieve spontaneous pregnancy within 12 mo without contraception. A male-associated factor is identified in 50% of couples who are involuntarily childless.
conditions.epidemiology: Approximately 15% of couples do not achieve pregnancy within 12 consecutive months and seek medical care. One in eight couples have difficulty conceiving a first child, and one in six have difficulty conceiving a subsequent child.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Abnormal semen parameters commonly accompany a male-associated factor, but semen analysis alone cannot distinguish fertile from infertile men.

subtypes.name: primary infertility
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Difficulty conceiving a first child.

subtypes.name: secondary infertility
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Difficulty conceiving a subsequent child.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify possible causes and relevant health, lifestyle and behavioural factors.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of men seeking help for fertility problems.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess male reproductive health, including testicular volume.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of men seeking help for fertility problems.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess semen and sperm characteristics using WHO reference values.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During the initial evaluation; obtain at least two consecutive analyses when the baseline result is abnormal.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: One analysis is sufficient if results meet WHO criteria. Abnormal results on at least two analyses warrant further andrological investigation. The 2021 lower reference limits (5th centile, with 95% CI) are semen volume 1.4 (1.3–1.5) ml; total sperm number 39 (35–40) 106/ejaculate; sperm concentration 16 (15–18) 106/ml; total motility 42 (40–43)%; progressive motility 30 (29–31)%; vitality 54 (50–56)%; and normal morphology 4 (3.9–4.0)%.

diagnostic_workup.test: Serum total testosterone, FSH and LH
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess hormonal status and detect hypogonadism.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At least in all cases of oligozoospermia and azoospermia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Estimate testicular volume.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of infertile men.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Examine testicular structure, identify tumours and assess possible signs of obstruction.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In men with infertility; particularly useful when clinical assessment of testicular volume is difficult.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Possible signs of obstruction include a dilated rete testis, an enlarged epididymis with cystic lesions, or an absent vas deferens.

diagnostic_workup.test: Female partner fertility assessment, including ovarian reserve
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform the timing and choice of treatment for the couple.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In parallel with diagnosis and management of the infertile male.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess oxidative stress.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Routine testing is not recommended.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Testing methods are not standardised and require further validation.

long_term_effects: Infertile men have increased risks of cardiometabolic disorders, cardiovascular mortality and overall mortality compared with fertile controls.
Infertile men have increased risks of testicular cancer and other cancers.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline advises counselling infertile men and men with abnormal semen parameters about associated health risks and screening infertile men for modifiable cardiovascular risk factors.

conditions.name: Idiopathic male infertility
conditions.description: The historical designation for impaired sperm parameters without an identified explanatory male-associated factor.
conditions.epidemiology: No explanatory male-associated factor is identified in 30–40% of cases.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Impaired sperm parameters without an identified underlying male-associated cause.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate potential monogenic causes and relevant genetic variants.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Its possible role in idiopathic infertility is discussed, but its clinical application is unclear.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Findings suggest potential diagnostic and management benefits, without an established clinical application.

conditions.name: Sperm DNA fragmentation
conditions.description: Reduced sperm DNA integrity is associated with poorer natural pregnancy rates and adverse outcomes after ART. Its effect on clinical management has not been unequivocally established by direct studies.
conditions.epidemiology: SDF is more common in infertile men.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Elevated SDF is associated with impaired embryo development, miscarriage, recurrent pregnancy loss and birth defects.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess sperm DNA integrity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: For couples with recurrent pregnancy loss after natural conception or failure of ART, and for men with unexplained infertility.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Current assays do not reliably predict ART outcomes, and routine clinical use remains controversial.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of common risk factors for elevated SDF
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify potentially addressable contributors.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before considering testicular sperm for ART in a man with high SDF.

conditions.name: Oligozoospermia
conditions.description: A sperm-count abnormality addressed in the guideline because it can affect the choice of hormonal and genetic investigations.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Reduced sperm numbers on semen analysis.

subtypes.name: idiopathic oligozoospermia
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Oligozoospermia without an identified cause; the guideline discusses FSH treatment when FSH values are within the normal range.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess sperm concentration and other semen parameters.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At initial evaluation and on at least two consecutive analyses if the baseline result is abnormal.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A sperm concentration of <5 million/ml identifies men for whom standard karyotype analysis is offered and Y-chromosome microdeletion testing is considered; the latter is described as mandatory at <1 million/ml in the accompanying text.

diagnostic_workup.test: Serum total testosterone, FSH and LH
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the hormonal profile.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In all cases of oligozoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: For idiopathic oligozoospermia, normal-range FSH is described as generally 1.5–8 mIU/ml.

diagnostic_workup.test: Standard karyotype analysis and genetic counselling
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify chromosomal abnormalities and inform reproductive counselling.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When spermatozoa are <5 million/ml.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The incidence of mainly autosomal structural abnormalities is 4% among patients with a sperm count <5 million/ml, described as tenfold higher than in the general population.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify Y-chromosome deletions relevant to fertility and counselling.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider for sperm concentrations of <5 million sperm/ml; the accompanying text describes testing as mandatory for concentrations <1 million/ml.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Deletions are rare above a sperm concentration of 5 million/ml and are relevant to reproductive prognosis and counselling.

conditions.name: Obstructive azoospermia
conditions.description: Absence of sperm from the ejaculate because the sperm transport pathway is blocked, rather than because spermatogenesis is abnormal.
conditions.epidemiology: OA accounts for 20–40% of azoospermia cases.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Typical findings include normal FSH, testes of normal size and low semen volume. An enlarged or dilated epididymis, epididymal or vasal nodules, and absent vas deferens in CBAVD may also occur.

subtypes.name: intratesticular obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Obstruction situated within the testis.

subtypes.name: epididymal obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Obstruction located in the epididymis.

subtypes.name: vasal obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Obstruction of the vas deferens, including obstruction following vasectomy.

subtypes.name: ejaculatory duct obstruction
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Distal obstruction that may follow inflammation or arise from a cyst.

subtypes.name: functional obstruction of the distal seminal ducts
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Functional impairment affecting the distal seminal ducts.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish azoospermia and assess semen volume.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During infertility assessment.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Low semen volume is a characteristic clinical finding of OA.

diagnostic_workup.test: FSH measurement and testicular volume assessment
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help characterise the cause of azoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of azoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Normal FSH and testicular size are characteristic of OA.

diagnostic_workup.test: Physical examination of the epididymis and vas deferens
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify dilation, nodules or absence of the vas deferens.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of azoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Absence of the vas deferens may indicate CBAVD.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the vas deferens, seminal vesicles, epididymis and indirect signs of obstruction.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During evaluation of suspected obstruction.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Findings may include rete testis dilation or an enlarged epididymis with cystic lesions.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate distal obstruction and abnormalities of the ejaculatory ducts or seminal vesicles.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: If partial or complete distal obstruction is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: It may identify ejaculatory duct cysts or obstruction and seminal-vesicle dilation, atrophy or hypoplasia.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform selection between reconstruction and sperm retrieval with ICSI.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When surgical reconstruction is being considered.

conditions.name: Nonobstructive azoospermia
conditions.description: Absence of sperm in the ejaculate after centrifugation in the setting of a severe spermatogenic deficit, often related to primary testicular dysfunction or dysfunction of the hypothalamuspituitary-gonadal axis.
conditions.epidemiology: Among patients with NOA, positive sperm retrieval after TESE has been reported in up to 50%, with substantial variation between cohorts and techniques.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Testicular volume is usually low, semen volume is usually normal and FSH is commonly high. Spermatogenesis may be confined to small, isolated testicular areas.

subtypes.name: Sertoli cell–only syndrome
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A testicular histological pattern associated with complete AZFa deletion.

subtypes.name: maturation arrest
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A testicular histological pattern that can coexist with normal FSH and testicular volume.

subtypes.name: hypospermatogenesis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A testicular histological pattern associated with better prediction of sperm retrieval than maturation arrest or Sertoli cell–only syndrome.

diagnostic_workup.test: Two consecutive semen analyses after centrifugation
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm absence of sperm in the ejaculate.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When NOA is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Confirm NOA when sperm are absent after centrifugation on two consecutive analyses.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate possible causes and associated comorbidity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During comprehensive assessment of NOA.

diagnostic_workup.test: Hormonal profile, including FSH and LH
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess endocrine function and possible causes.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During comprehensive assessment of NOA.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: FSH is commonly high, but FSH alone does not accurately predict whether spermatogenesis is present at TESE.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate a possible association with sperm retrieval outcome.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Discussed in men undergoing mTESE; it is not established as a reliable stand-alone predictor.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Growing evidence associates lower preoperative serum AMH with a higher likelihood of positive sperm retrieval.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess testicular anatomy, volume and associated abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During comprehensive assessment of NOA.

diagnostic_workup.test: Standard karyotype analysis and genetic counselling
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify chromosomal abnormalities and inform reproductive decisions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In all men with azoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: NOA has the highest prevalence of chromosomal abnormalities among the degrees of spermatogenic dysfunction discussed.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify deletions that affect sperm retrieval prognosis and counselling.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In men with azoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Complete deletions involving AZFa and AZFb indicate an almost zero likelihood of sperm retrieval.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Characterise the spermatogenic pattern when tissue is obtained.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In the context of testicular procedures.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Hypospermatogenesis predicts positive sperm retrieval more accurately than maturation arrest or Sertoli cell–only syndrome.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate possible monogenic causes and relevant genetic variants.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Its potential introduction for NOA is discussed, but its clinical application remains unclear.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The diagnostic yield is increasing, without a clearly established clinical application.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Locate sites that might have a higher probability of yielding sperm.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: It is not recommended as a primary diagnostic or pre-TESE prognostic procedure.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Mapping does not itself retrieve sperm; comparative RCTs and effective cost/benefit analyses are lacking.

pathology_markers.clinical_significance: Compared with maturation arrest or SCOS, this histological pattern was more accurate in predicting positive sperm retrieval after TESE.
Normal FSH and testicular volume do not exclude this histological pattern.
Complete AZFa deletion is associated with this histological pattern.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Complete deletion is associated with SCOS and poor surgical sperm retrieval prognosis.
Complete deletion is associated with spermatogenic arrest and poor surgical sperm retrieval prognosis.
Deletion may present as oligospermia or azoospermia; TESE retrieves sperm in 53–75% of affected men.

conditions.name: Klinefelter syndrome
conditions.description: A chromosomal condition characterised by additional X chromosomes and variable clinical findings.
conditions.epidemiology: The clinical presentation and the presence of germ cells or spermatogenesis vary; TESE can retrieve sperm in 20–50% of cases.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The guideline describes variable manifestations and variable preservation of spermatogenesis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify the chromosomal abnormality.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In men with azoospermia or spermatozoa <5 million/ml.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Klinefelter syndrome is represented in the document as 47, XXY.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: The additional X chromosome is a chromosomal cause of male infertility.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline recommends appropriate medical treatment alongside endocrine follow-up.

conditions.name: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens
conditions.description: A structural absence of both vasa deferentia that can cause obstructive azoospermia and may result from a CFTR alteration.
conditions.epidemiology: CBAVD is detected in approximately 1% of infertile men and in up to 6% of men with OA.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Azoospermia with absent vas deferens; low semen volume and acidic pH are particularly relevant findings during assessment.

diagnostic_workup.test: Physical examination of the vas deferens
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify absence of the vas deferens.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In all men with azoospermia, particularly when semen volume is <1.0 ml and pH is <7.0.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify findings that increase suspicion of CBAVD.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of azoospermia.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Semen volume <1.0 ml and acidic pH <7.0 warrant particular attention to possible CBAVD.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess whether the vas deferens and seminal vesicles are present and identify associated epididymal abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During imaging assessment of suspected structural obstruction.

diagnostic_workup.test: CFTR mutation testing in the man and his partner
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify relevant inherited genetic alterations.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: For structural abnormalities involving unilateral or bilateral absence of the vas deferens without renal anomalies.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Any CFTR alteration may lead to CBAVD.

genetic_molecular.clinical_significance: Alterations may cause CBAVD; the guideline reports approximately 2000 identified CFTR mutations.

conditions.name: Cryptorchidism
conditions.description: A maldescended testis may undergo germ-cell loss beginning after the first year of life, with further decline during the second year. It has been postulated as a possible component of TDS.
conditions.epidemiology: Cryptorchidism affects approximately 1% of infants. Compared with the general population, men with cryptorchidism have a 3.6–7.4 times higher risk of a germ cell tumour; 2–6% of men with a history of cryptorchidism develop a testicular tumour.
conditions.clinical_presentation: A unilateral undescended testis may coexist with structural abnormalities in the normally descended contralateral testis. Men with previous bilateral cryptorchidism have a paternity rate of 35–53%, whereas paternity after unilateral cryptorchidism is nearly equivalent to that in men without cryptorchidism.

subtypes.name: unilateral cryptorchidism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: One testis is undescended; the contralateral descended testis may also have structural or fertility-related abnormalities.

subtypes.name: bilateral cryptorchidism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Both testes are undescended; a history of this condition is associated with a paternity rate of 35–53%.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Guide management of adult cryptorchidism and assess contralateral testicular function.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In adults with an undescended testis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Biochemical hypogonadism or impaired sperm production affects consideration of orchidopexy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect intratesticular GCNIS.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When an undescended testis is corrected in adulthood.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: GCNIS is a prognostic indicator for later TGCT.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for GCNIS.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At orchidectomy for TGCT in patients at high risk for GCNIS, including those with a history of cryptorchidism.

pathology_markers.clinical_significance: Its detection in an undescended testis informs prognosis for future TGCT.

long_term_effects: Increased risk of testicular cancer, which remains higher than in men without cryptorchidism even after early orchidopexy.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Patients and parents should be counselled that unilateral disease may also affect the contralateral testis; those with bilateral disease should be counselled about the reported paternity rate.

conditions.name: Testicular germ cell tumour
conditions.description: A testicular malignancy relevant to infertility assessment, fertility preservation and long-term health after treatment.
conditions.epidemiology: TGCT is the most common malignancy among Caucasian men aged 15–40 yr and affects approximately 1% of subfertile men. The average 10-yr survival rate for testicular cancer is 98%. In men with TGCT, azoospermia has been observed in 24% and oligospermia in 50%.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Semen quality may be reduced before cancer treatment. Following treatment, additional impairment of spermatogenesis and Leydig cell function may occur.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess fertility status and identify azoospermia or severe semen abnormalities before treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before planned cancer treatment and when considering fertility preservation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify and characterise a testicular lesion.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of infertile men or suspected testicular abnormalities.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: No definitive lesion-size criterion separates benign from malignant findings. A lesion < 5 mm is more likely to be benign, according to cited data.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Distinguish benign from malignant testicular lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When tissue diagnosis is pursued after assessment of an indeterminate or suspicious lesion.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Histology remains the clinical standard for this distinction.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect GCNIS.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At orchidectomy for TGCT in patients at high risk for GCNIS, including those with cryptorchidism, testicular volume <12 ml or hypospermatogenesis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess hypogonadism during management.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During management of patients with TGCT.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The risk of hypogonadism is greatest at 6–12 mo after treatment and may subsequently improve.

pathology_markers.clinical_significance: Assessment may be relevant in a contralateral testis with risk factors.

follow_up.schedule: Long-term management through a dedicated late-effects clinic and survivorship programme is recommended; no visit interval is specified.
long_term_effects: Increased risks of hypogonadism, sexual dysfunction and cardiovascular disease.
Sperm aneuploidy may remain increased for up to 2 yr following gonadotoxic therapy.
Spermatogenesis usually recovers 1–4 yr after chemotherapy.
Chemotherapy is associated with DNA damage and increased SDF.
Sperm aneuploidy often returns to pretreatment levels 18–24 mo after treatment.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Management is recommended in a multidisciplinary setting. Because Leydig cell function may improve after treatment, the guideline considers it reasonable to defer testosterone therapy until signs or symptoms of deficiency persist.

conditions.name: Testicular microcalcification
conditions.description: A testicular parenchymal finding whose association with TGCT is considered controversial and depends on accompanying risk factors.
conditions.epidemiology: Microcalcification is found in 0.6–9% of men referred for testicular US. A cited meta-analysis found a higher risk of concurrent TGCT in men with TM and a history of subfertility, cryptorchidism or previous TGCT (risk ratio 8.5, 95% CI 4.5–16.1; p < 0.0001). A separate systematic review and meta-analysis reported higher odds of testicular cancer among infertile men with TM (pooled OR 18.11, 95% CI 8.09–40.55; p < 0.0001).
conditions.clinical_presentation: TM may occur in otherwise healthy, asymptomatic men or alongside infertility, cryptorchidism, TGCT and other testicular conditions.

subtypes.name: isolated TM
subtypes.distinguishing_features: TM without accompanying risk factors such as infertility, cryptorchidism, testicular cancer or an atrophic testis.

subtypes.name: TM with associated lesions
subtypes.distinguishing_features: TM accompanied by a lesion that may require assessment for suspicious examination or US findings.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify microcalcification and assess any accompanying lesion.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During imaging evaluation of testicular findings.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Associated lesion characteristics, including size, echogenicity, vascularity and interval growth, inform malignancy risk assessment.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess men at higher risk for GCNIS or TGCT.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Offered to infertile men with TM in specified higher-risk groups; not recommended for isolated TM without associated risk factors.

diagnostic_workup.test: Follow-up scrotal US, biochemical tumour markers, or abdominal or pelvic computed tomography
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate or monitor possible malignancy.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: These investigations are not recommended for isolated TM without associated risk factors.

pathology_markers.clinical_significance: Identifying men who may harbour GCNIS is a consideration when TM coexists with risk factors.

follow_up.schedule: Self-examination is advised even without additional risk factors; no interval is specified.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: For isolated TM without associated risk factors, the guideline advises against follow-up scrotal US and the other specified malignancy investigations.

conditions.name: Varicocele
conditions.description: A condition commonly identified on physical examination; the exact relationship between varicocele and reduced male fertility remains unknown.
conditions.epidemiology: Varicocele is present in almost 15% of the normal male population, 25% of men with abnormal semen analysis and 35– 40% of men presenting with infertility.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Worse semen parameters are associated with higher varicocele grade and age.

subtypes.name: clinical varicocele
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A varicocele detected clinically, for which treatment is considered in specified infertility settings.

subtypes.name: subclinical varicocele
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Treatment was not effective at increasing spontaneous pregnancy in the evidence discussed.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect a varicocele.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of male infertility.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm a varicocele and assess venous diameter and reflux.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When imaging confirmation or additional measurements are needed.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Radiologically significant findings comprise venous diameter >3 mm both upright and during the Valsalva manoeuvre, with reflux lasting more than 2 s.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess whether semen parameters are abnormal when deciding on management.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During infertility evaluation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline advises against treating varicocele in infertile men whose semen analysis is normal.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess DNA fragmentation in relevant infertility or ART-failure settings.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As specified for recurrent pregnancy loss, ART failure or unexplained infertility.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The evidence for benefit from varicocele treatment solely because SDF is abnormal remains limited.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of female partner ovarian reserve
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform the couple's treatment decisions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When considering varicocele treatment, particularly for couples in which ovarian reserve may be limited.

follow_up.schedule: After repair, improvement in semen parameters takes up to two spermatogenic cycles on average; spontaneous pregnancy has been reported between 6 and 12 mo after varicocelectomy.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline states that the evidence for repair in NOA is of low quality and calls for discussion of risks and benefits, particularly when the female partner has limited ovarian reserve.

conditions.name: Male accessory-gland infections
conditions.description: The conditions grouped under this designation according to WHO are urethritis, prostatitis, orchitis and epididymitis.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The effects of symptomatic and asymptomatic infections on sperm quality are contradictory; available evidence did not establish a strong association between sexually transmitted infections and male infertility.

subtypes.name: chronic bacterial prostatitis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Identified as type II in the National Institutes of Health classification; the guideline reports symptomatic and microbiological responses to antibiotics.

diagnostic_workup.test: Peroxidase-positive white blood cell count in ejaculate
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify an inflammatory process.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During evaluation of suspected genital-tract inflammation or infection.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A level >106/ml of ejaculate indicates inflammation but does not by itself establish infection.

diagnostic_workup.test: Semen culture or polymerase chain reaction analysis
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate common urinary tract pathogens.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In all suspected cases of genitourinary tract infection.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A pathogen concentration >103 CFU/ml in ejaculate indicates significant bacteriospermia.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: Sexual partners should be referred for evaluation and treatment when an accessory sex gland infection is known or suspected to result from a sexually transmitted disease.

conditions.name: Leukocytospermia
conditions.description: An elevated count of peroxidase-positive white blood cells in ejaculate that indicates inflammation without necessarily indicating infection.
conditions.clinical_presentation: A cited meta-analysis found no association with reduced fertility after ART or altered semen quality among men without symptoms of genital-tract infection who sought care for couple subfertility.

diagnostic_workup.test: Peroxidase-positive white blood cell count in ejaculate
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect leukocytospermia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When investigating suspected inflammation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A level >106/ml of ejaculate indicates an inflammatory process, not necessarily infection.

diagnostic_workup.test: Semen culture or polymerase chain reaction analysis
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify common urinary tract pathogens if infection is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In suspected genitourinary tract infection.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A pathogen concentration >103 CFU/ml in ejaculate indicates significant bacteriospermia.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The document states that evidence does not show improved conception rates from treating leukocytospermia alone when infective organisms have not been identified.

conditions.name: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
conditions.description: A form of hypogonadism for which the guideline discusses inducing spermatogenesis in men seeking to conceive.
conditions.clinical_presentation: It may be congenital or acquired and can coexist with azoospermia.

subtypes.name: Kallmann syndrome
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Listed among causes of secondary (hypogonadotropic) hypogonadism.

subtypes.name: Idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Listed among causes of secondary (hypogonadotropic) hypogonadism.

diagnostic_workup.test: Serum total testosterone, FSH and LH
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess hormonal status in an infertile man.
